# Draft:Bluejay (ESC firmware)

----
Bluejay is an open-source electronic speed controller (ESC) firmware used primarily with multirotor flight controllers and ESCs originally designed for BLHeli_S firmware. Bluejay is commonly referenced in the FPV ecosystem for enabling features such as bidirectional DShot telemetry on some BLHeli_S-class ESCs, which can be used for RPM-based filtering and related telemetry features in compatible flight-controller firmware.
History
Bluejay is a community-maintained open-source successor-style firmware project that is based on BLHeli_S revision 16.7 and targets Busy Bee-class microcontrollers used in many 8-bit ESCs. Bird Sanctuary describes the organization as maintaining and advancing the Bluejay firmware project.
Features
Bluejay is commonly used to enable or improve integration with flight-controller firmware that supports ESC telemetry features. Betaflight documentation describes Bluejay as a BLHeli_S firmware option and notes bidirectional DShot availability on BLHeli_S when using Bluejay.
Betaflight’s manufacturer design guidance also references Bluejay as a preferred option for BLHeli_S ESCs in certain integrated hardware contexts.
Independent FPV documentation and guides also describe Bluejay as a firmware that can enable higher PWM frequency options and bidirectional DShot/RPM filtering on BLHeli_S ESCs.
Flashing and configuration tools
Bluejay is commonly flashed to compatible ESCs using tools that support BLHeli_S passthrough workflows. Betaflight documentation notes that Bluejay can be flashed using the web-based ESC Configurator.
* ESC Configurator (web tool) supports flashing Bluejay on supported ESCs.
* Prober is an open-source flashing tool that supports Bluejay workflows (including packaged firmware selection in its distribution).
Distribution
Bluejay releases are distributed as source code and as precompiled firmware images (for example, Intel HEX files) published on the project’s release pages.
